title: Project A — Accessible Vue Application
summary: Build a small Vue application (booking form + dialog workflow) that is accessible by construction, then prove it with manual keyboard/screen-reader audits and automated a11y tests.
requirements: Vue 3 <script setup> + TypeScript + Pinia for the booking state
Semantic HTML throughout: landmarks, native controls, one h1 per page
Every form field: label, hint, and error wired via aria-describedby, errors announced with role=alert
A modal confirmation dialog with focus trap, Escape-to-close, and focus restore
A tabbed section implemented with the tablist/tab/tabpanel pattern and arrow-key navigation
WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark themes; visible :focus-visible styles
Manual audit documented: keyboard-only walkthrough findings and fixes
Vitest + axe assertions: zero violations, error announcements asserted behaviorally

hints: Run the keyboard walkthrough BEFORE writing tests — structural fixes change markup, not just attributes.
The focus trap only needs: keydown Tab listener, first/last focusable detection, and saved document.activeElement.
axe catches missing labels/contrast; the announcements (role=alert, aria-live) need behavioral tests.
completionCriteria: Keyboard-only user can complete the booking flow end-to-end
axe reports zero violations in both themes
Every form error is announced (asserted by test)
